name: Molybdenum Deficiency
description: Molybdenum is a micronutrient essential for nitrogen metabolism and nitrogen fixation in legumes. Deficiency causes symptoms similar to nitrogen deficiency and characteristic whiptail in brassicas.
symptoms: Whip tail in leafy vegetables (narrow, distorted leaves)
Poor nodulation in legumes and reduced nitrogen fixation
causes: Low available molybdenum in acidic soils (pH <5.5)
treatments: Foliar spray of sodium or ammonium molybdate (0.05-0.1%)
Apply molybdenum trioxide or sodium molybdate to soil
Treat legume seeds with molybdenum (1g Mo per kg seed) before planting
Apply lime to raise pH, which increases molybdenum availability
prevention: Maintain soil pH at 6.0-7.0 through liming
Include molybdenum in micronutrient blends for acid soils
Apply small amounts (100-200 g/ha Mo) which are usually sufficient
